subject: Vendor risk follow-up: subprocessor boundaries & compliance evidence
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lisa Moreno <lisa.moreno@finedgeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor security & subprocessor follow-up

Hi Lisa,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciated the time. As requested, I wanted to follow up with our initial artifacts and a proposed cadence for next steps so your risk team can progress the vendor review. Key items below: 

- What I attached: "Redwood_Subprocessors_2026.pdf" (current list and short descriptions), and a short note on where processing happens.
- Evidence we can provide quickly: SOC 2 Type II attestation, system inventory exports, and a concise data flow diagram (we'll produce a one-page diagram for your reviewer).
- Quick answers: hosted API runs primarily in AWS us-west-2 for production; backups replicate to GCP in us-east1 for disaster recovery; we use managed Redis/ElastiCache for state caching.

Questions from your checklist I flagged during the call:
1) Do you need the full SOC 2 report or redacted attestation first?
2) Any specific DPIA/GDPR artifacts beyond processing descriptions?
3) Are there particular subprocessors you want more detail about (e.g., KMS, analytics)?

Proposed next steps:
- You: confirm which artifacts you want first (attestation vs full report).
- Us: Marissa will drop the SOC 2 cert and Karthik will provide the network/data-flow diagram by end of day Wed (6/17).
- We'll set a follow-up call Thursday if your team needs a walkthrough.

Attachments: Redwood_Subprocessors_2026.pdf (subprocessor list, zones, and data categories).

If helpful I can also open a shared Drive folder and send a HubSpot link for the deal so your procurement team can track docs.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Lisa Moreno <lisa.moreno@finedgeanalytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor security & subprocessor follow-up

Jordan —

Thanks, this is helpful. I attached our vendor security worksheet (FEA-Vendor-Security-RQ-Answers.xlsx) with the initial items we can skip vs. require. A few quick clarifications:

- SOC 2: We typically ask for the attestation first and the full report (redacted) for high-risk vendors. Please send the attestation and we can request the full report if needed.
- Data flow: We need a one-page diagram showing where PII and embeddings are stored and which subprocessors have access to them.
- GDPR/HIPAA: At this stage, we need confirmation on whether Redwood has any data processing agreements in place and whether you support data residency options.

Two short questions for your team:
1) For hosted API, are tokens or embeddings stored beyond 30 days?
2) Which KMS is used for encryption of stored embeddings?

If you can provide the SOC attestation and the one-page data flow by Wednesday, we can keep the review on track. Looping in our security mailbox for visibility: security@finedgeanalytics.com.

Thanks,
Lisa Moreno
Senior Security Analyst
FinEdge Analytics
lisa.moreno@finedgeanalytics.com
Attachment: FEA-Vendor-Security-RQ-Answers.xlsx

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Vendor security & subprocessor follow-up

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding FinEdge's note and worksheet. They want the SOC attestation and a one-page data flow by EOD Wed. Quick plan:

- Marissa: can you confirm we can share the 2025 SOC 2 Type II attestation and whether we should produce a redacted version? They prefer attestation first.
- Karthik: can you produce a one-page data flow that calls out: hosting region (AWS us-west-2), backups to GCP us-east1, storage of embeddings (encrypted S3), and which managed services have production access (KMS, Redis/ElastiCache, CloudSQL). Also flag any subprocessors that will need separate questionnaires (e.g., analytics or observability vendors).
- I'll create the shared Drive folder and send the HubSpot link to Lisa once we have the two artifacts.

Please keep replies short — this is timeboxed.

Hi Lisa / Security team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few updates and next steps:

- Attached: SOC attestation (SOC2_Redwood_2025_Type2.pdf) — this is the attestation Marissa mentioned.
- Pending: Karthik is finishing the one-page data flow diagram (will call out: PII never stored beyond session logs for traceability, embeddings are stored encrypted in AWS S3 with AWS KMS; backups replicate to GCP us-east1 and are encrypted; managed services with production access include AWS KMS, ElastiCache, and CloudSQL).
- Subprocessors: see attached Redwood_Subprocessors_2026.pdf for full list and short descriptions (we highlighted the cloud providers and any analytics/observability vendors).

Proposed timeline:
1) Today: we share SOC attestation and subprocessor list (done).
2) By EOD tomorrow: one-page data flow diagram from Karthik.
3) If you need the full SOC report: let us know and we will coordinate secure delivery and redaction.
